newsitem.title: UK: Oil price slides further as Iraqi exports rise.
newsitem.headline: Oil price slides further as Iraqi exports rise.

text.p: Oil prices slipped again on Monday and showed little sign of reversing the headlong slide which already has cut the value of crude by 20 percent this year.
International benchmark Brent blend futures for April delivery traded down 16 cents at $19.63 a barrel. Brent has fallen $5 in six weeks after hitting six-year highs late last year.
Dealers said falling prices were forcing Iraq to export more to meet the cash target permitted under the United Nations oil-for-food exchange which started in December.
Iraq is allowed to export a billion dollars' worth of crude by March 9, followed by a second billion by early June when the exchange comes up for review at the U.N.
"The effect is to destabilise the market," said a trader. "The more Iraq sells the more the price falls and the more Iraq must sell to hit its target."
Iraqi crude now is fetching only $18 a barrel in Europe compared to $23 when Baghdad moved its first exports under the deal in mid-December.
Dealers said continued mild northern hemisphere winter weather had stunted demand for heating oil and allowed global inventories to recover.
Forecaster Weather Services Corp predicted "above average temperatures" throughout Europe for the rest of this week.
The United States also was expected to see warmer weather after a shortlived cold spell this week.
"Notwithstanding freakish weather conditions or major refinery problems, the market should be adequately supplied over the next month or two," said brokers GNI in a report.
